assessment_summary: Step 0016 contains a logical error. It claims that for the prefix \hat\sigma = \sigma[..i], any infinite extension \sigma' will fail to satisfy (P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow \mathsf{F}(P1C \vee P2C) at step i. This is false because an extension could easily have P1C or P2C be true at some step j > i, thereby satisfying the future operator \mathsf{F} and making the implication true. Therefore, \hat\sigma is not a bad prefix, and the proof that it is a safety property fails.
